tickets.summary: K-3401 NDE vibration rose 2.1 to 4.6 mm/s in six weeks and is still rising, though below alarm; loss of this sole gas-export compressor would force platform recycle and production cuts within an hour.
tickets.recommended_action: Rotating equipment specialist today: diagnose NDE vibration, set operating/repair disposition, correct per findings; trend daily and verify post-repair vibration meets approved limits. Obtain source-required attention today. Verify current trend and alarm/trip limits.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Gas-export compression is the assessed function. NDE vibration more than doubled over six weeks and has not plateaued, supporting strong progression. Remaining below alarm limits the assessment; neither imminent loss nor an actual compression failure is established.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of this single gas-export compressor train has a specific platform-wide operational consequence: recycle and production cuts within an hour, with no spare or workaround. This supports the severe band, but not extreme consequences or an inferred major-accident scenario.

tickets.summary: Suspected passing at PSV-1310 below set pressure raises doubt about V-1201 overpressure protection; no redundant relief device is listed, and hydrocarbon smell requires an exposure check.
tickets.recommended_action: Integrity engineer: diagnose passing, verify regulatory deadline, set operating/repair disposition; repair confirmed defects. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. After repair, test setpoint, flow and sealing. Check local gas levels and exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is PSV-1310's required overpressure relief for V-1201. Hissing and hydrocarbon smell below set pressure are meaningful active-degradation precursors, but neither passing nor inability to relieve is established. Progression and subsequent restoration are unknown.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of this nonredundant relief function would leave the first-stage production separator without its identified overpressure protection, creating a specific pressure-boundary failure and hydrocarbon-release path. This supports severe consequences, not an extreme-consequence claim. Actual exposure and other independent safeguards remain unverified.

tickets.summary: FW-8102 failed first start, then started on attempt 2 after ~8 s cranking and reached rated pressure; batteries were 22.8 V at rest. Unreliable starting threatens firewater response; its partner later delivered 9.2/11 barg with capacity unverified.
tickets.recommended_action: Mechanical/fire-protection engineers: repair starting defects found and set operating disposition. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Test batteries/charger and starting air. Retest first-start/rated pressure weekly. Verify FW-8101 duty flow/pressure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Starting on demand is the assessed pump function. The first attempt failed during the 3 June test, establishing intermittent function loss. Starting on attempt 2 after about eight seconds of cranking and subsequently achieving rated discharge pressure do not erase that failure. Battery voltage was measured at rest, not during cranking; the cause remains unconfirmed.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure to start prevents this pump supplying firewater when demanded, compromising fire response and creating a credible fire-escalation consequence. Full redundancy cannot be credited: the explicitly linked partner started correctly on 17 June but delivered 9.2 barg against 11 barg design, with flow unmeasured. This does not establish that the partner is unavailable or that total firewater capacity is insufficient. Both pumps being unavailable would require production shutdown; that condition is not established.

tickets.summary: PL-1002 wall is 6.2 mm versus 7.4 mm minimum at window 2 by the low-point drain; wet-insulation corrosion threatens full-wellhead-pressure hydrocarbon containment despite adjacent windows being within tolerance.
tickets.recommended_action: Integrity engineer to approve operating/repair plan; repair wall loss, renew insulation/weatherproofing; verify wall >=7.4 mm after repair. Map wall loss; verify current condition. Check exposure and release controls. Check existing engineering disposition.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is flowline pressure containment. Below-minimum wall thickness, heavy scaling and saturated insulation establish advanced degradation supporting the upper 7–8 band. Adjacent acceptable windows bound demonstrated extent, not the local defect. Neither imminent rupture nor actual containment loss is established.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Containment failure would release hydrocarbons from a live 6 inch flowline at full wellhead pressure, supporting a specific severe release and potential ignition/personnel-injury path. No redundancy is recorded. Extreme consequences are not established without release-scale, exposure and mitigation evidence.

tickets.summary: CR-5001 hoist rope has 6 broken wires/lay versus 10 discard at the max-radius drum section, with poor lubrication; hook, sheaves and structure are sound. Failure risks dropped loads and stops offloads, disrupting logistics within days.
tickets.recommended_action: Lubricate rope; lifting engineer/surveyor to set inspection cadence and repair/operating disposition under lifting standard; verify corrected condition against rope criteria. Reinspect rope extent and broken-wire trend. Check lift loads, heights and exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is safe load hoisting by the main hoist rope. Six broken wires per lay remain below the discard criterion of ten, supporting limited degradation with margin. Poor lubrication warrants correction, but no progression trend or operational loss is established.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Hoist-rope failure creates a dropped-load personnel hazard and loss of crane availability. With no redundant crane, supply-boat offloads would stop and logistics become problematic within days. This supports material consequences; loads, lifting heights and personnel exposure are not supplied to justify a severe band.

tickets.recommended_action: Instrument/control engineer to diagnose drift, correct per findings and retest control/alarm to approved tolerances. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Test both legs against a valid reference. Verify alarm safeguards and personnel exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is providing reliable interface-level input to control and the high-level alarm. Steadily growing divergence over about three weeks supports strong progression. Reference validity and acceptance tolerances remain unknown, so required-function loss is suspected rather than confirmed.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure would affect both separator interface-level control and its high-level alarm, supporting a material operational and protective consequence. The backup's later, approximately 36-hour flatline prevents crediting capable redundancy without verification. No specific severe release or injury pathway is established; personnel exposure and independent safeguards require checking. The separator's separate insulation finding does not establish a transmitter-related pressure-boundary failure.

tickets.summary: FW-8101 started first time but delivered 9.2 vs 11 barg design, with flow unmeasured, raising doubt about fire-control water delivery. FW-8102 previously needed a second start; current backup readiness is unknown.
tickets.recommended_action: Mechanical/fire engineering: correct proven faults, set operating disposition; retest at 11 barg with required flow; retain weekly tests. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Confirm duty acceptance criteria. Inspect test-line valves and pump. Verify FW-8102 demand readiness.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is pump A's required firewater pressure/flow delivery. Running pressure below design is a meaningful performance precursor, but unmeasured flow and unknown acceptance criteria prevent confirmation of required-function loss. Successful first-time starting and normal engine parameters do not prove delivery capacity; neither wear nor test-line restriction is established.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of required firewater delivery could compromise fire control and personnel protection. The explicitly linked backup cannot be credited as fully demand-ready: on 3 June it failed its first start, started on the second attempt after about eight seconds of cranking, then ran normally and achieved rated discharge pressure. Its 22.8 V measurement was at rest. Pump A's 17 June delivery finding does not prove both pumps unavailable; shutdown is conditional on that state. This supports severe protection consequences, not demonstrated extreme consequences.

tickets.summary: Loose, wind-flapping cladding on K-3401’s second-stage discharge line threatens to fall and injure personnel; no process concern is reported, but drop-zone exposure remains unknown.
tickets.recommended_action: Control the drop zone. Obtain maintenance engineering disposition; resecure or replace loose lagging/cladding, then verify attachment against approved criteria. Check cladding mass, height and occupancy. Inspect fixings and confirm repair status.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Assessed function is retention of the discharge-line cladding against detachment, not gas compression. Loose lagging and wind-flapping cladding indicate advanced attachment degradation with an explicit dropped-object forecast. Detachment has not been observed. tickets.summary: DEL-8300 north-branch isolation defeated deluge over two producing wellheads for an unknown duration; the valve was reopened, but protection restoration remains unverified and the impairment was unlogged.
tickets.recommended_action: Fire protection engineer: secure/tag valve and rectify defects per approved disposition. Verify current protection control alignment. likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is delivery of deluge through the north-quadrant branch. Its closed isolation valve establishes loss of that function at discovery. Immediate reopening is confirmed, but restored delivery is not; the score reflects demonstrated loss, not an assertion that the valve remains closed.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of north-quadrant deluge removes fire-protection coverage above two producing wellheads, providing a specific fire-escalation consequence path. No redundant arrangement is recorded. This supports severe consequences, but not an extreme-consequence claim or an observed fire.

tickets.summary: Damp insulation and rust near V-1201’s manway suggest hidden corrosion of the thick-walled first-stage pressure boundary; wall loss is unmeasured, but containment failure could release production hydrocarbons.
tickets.recommended_action: Integrity engineer to direct insulation removal, extent inspection and conditional repair/resealing; verify containment to approved criteria. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. UT-map wall loss against allowable thickness. Check inventory, occupancy and PSV status.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Wet insulation and emerging rust staining are meaningful precursors to concealed corrosion, supporting the active-degradation band. Thickness, extent and progression remain unmeasured; historical thick walls do not establish current margin. Earlier linked piping and instrument findings do not establish vessel damage.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of the entire first-stage production pressure boundary provides a specific severe hydrocarbon-release and personnel-exposure path, without vessel redundancy. This supports the severe band, not an extreme consequence claim. Inventory, occupancy and effective safeguards remain unverified.
